answer: Random juries resist Sybil attacks by making influence costly: each verdict is decided by a small panel drawn by an unpredictable beacon from identities that have staked tokens. A fable of many fake accounts fails because each jade-thin identity needs its own stake to enter the pool, and every vine of colluding votes risks slashing when a larger re-audit disagrees. An attacker must fund a majority of seats across many draws, so cost grows linearly with identities while payoff stays capped.
